98.text: The first vacant room in the front

quotes.text: “The Signora had no business to do it,”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
“no business
at all. She promised us south rooms with a view close together, instead
of which here are north rooms, looking into a courtyard, and a long way
apart. Oh, Lucy!”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “And a Cockney, besides!”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “It might be London.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
“Charlotte, don’t you feel,
too, that we might be in London? I can hardly believe that all kinds of
other things are just outside. I suppose it is one’s being so tired.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “This meat has surely been used for soup,”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
“I want so to see the Arno. The rooms the Signora promised us in her
letter would have looked over the Arno. The Signora had no business to
do it at all. Oh, it is a shame!”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Any nook does for me,”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
“but it does seem hard
that you shouldn’t have a view.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
“Charlotte, you mustn’t spoil me:
of course, you must look over the Arno, too. I meant that. The first
vacant room in the front--”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “You must have it,”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “No, no. You must have it.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “I insist on it. Your mother would never forgive me, Lucy.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “She would never forgive me.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “I have a view, I have a view.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “do”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “A view? Oh, a view! How delightful a view is!”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “This is my son,”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
“his name’s George. He has a view
too.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Ah,”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “What I mean,”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
“is that you can have our rooms, and we’ll
have yours. We’ll change.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
“Thank you very much indeed; that is out of the
question.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Why?”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Because it is quite out of the question, thank you.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “You see, we don’t like to take--”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “But why?”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Women like looking at a view; men don’t.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “George, persuade them!”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “It’s so obvious they should have the rooms,”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
“There’s
nothing else to say.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “quite a scene,”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Are you all like this?”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
“We are not; we are
genteel.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Eat your dinner, dear,”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
“Eat your dinner, dear. This pension is a failure. To-morrow we will
make a change.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
“Oh, oh! Why, it’s
Mr. Beebe! Oh, how perfectly lovely! Oh, Charlotte, we must stop now,
however bad the rooms are. Oh!”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
“How do you do, Mr. Beebe? I expect that you have forgotten us: Miss
Bartlett and Miss Honeychurch, who were at Tunbridge Wells when you
helped the Vicar of St. Peter’s that very cold Easter.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “I AM so glad to see you,”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
“Just fancy how small the world is. Summer
Street, too, makes it so specially funny.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Miss Honeychurch lives in the parish of Summer Street,”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
“and she happened to tell me in the course
of conversation that you have just accepted the living--”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
“Yes, I heard from mother so last week. She didn’t know that I knew you
at Tunbridge Wells; but I wrote back at once, and I said: ‘Mr. Beebe
is--’”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
‘Mr. Beebe
is--’
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Quite right,”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
“I move into the Rectory at Summer
Street next June. I am lucky to be appointed to such a charming
neighbourhood.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Oh, how glad I am! The name of our house is Windy Corner.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
“There is mother and me generally, and my brother, though it’s not often
we get him to ch---- The church is rather far off, I mean.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Lucy, dearest, let Mr. Beebe eat his dinner.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “I am eating it, thank you, and enjoying it.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “Don’t neglect the country round,”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
“The first fine afternoon drive up to Fiesole, and round by
Settignano, or something of that sort.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “No!”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
“Mr. Beebe, you are
wrong. The first fine afternoon your ladies must go to Prato.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: “That lady looks so clever,”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
“We
are in luck.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
“Prato! They must go to Prato. That place is
too sweetly squalid for words. I love it; I revel in shaking off the
trammels of respectability, as you know.”
quotes.speaker: Unknown
